review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–135. It has no new definitions, structures, classes or instances. It has one theorem, `KTheory.K0.traceModCommutators_map`, which states that the Hattori–Stallings trace is natural under extension of scalars. The statement uses Mathlib's `QuotientAddGroup.map` directly, and the proof is built from existing Mathlib operations such as `LinearMap.fst`, `LinearMap.inl` and `Matrix.trace`. The helper names it uses (`Ring.additiveCommutators`, `traceModCommutators`, `ModuleCat.RightExtension.*`, `Module.rightFreeCoordEquiv`) come from other project files, not from this one. I did not check whether those concepts duplicate Mathlib, because they are outside this file. The rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication and proof shortening, so there is no competing concept to assess in this file. The statement and the proof both repeat the same closure-based proof that `Ring.additiveCommutators R` maps into `Ring.additiveCommutators S`. That is a proof-structure issue, not a duplicate concept.
